newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hongkong exodus expected as 1997 nears - paper.
newsitem.headline: Hongkong exodus expected as 1997 nears - paper.

text.p: Emigration from Hong Kong will surge this year as the British colony braces for its 1997 return to Chinese rule, the South China Morning Post said on Thursday.
With 292 days until the handover, Hong Kong government figures showed the level of emigration will jump 23 percent, it said.

Up to 53,000 people would leave Hong Kong this year, up from 43,000 the previous year, and nearing the level of emigration seen in the aftermath of China's 1989 crackdown on student-led demonstrations in Tiananmen Square, the paper said.
Hong Kong government officials were not immediately available for comment.
An independent survey of Hong Kong's brain drain, issued this week, said most of those who emigrated did so because of uncertainties surrounding the handover.
While the survey, by the Institute of Human Resources Management, showed the brain drain slowed last year by 26 percent, its authors said emigration could surge again closer to the handover.

Another study, tracking attitudes of Hong Kong people towards the handover, has shown that more than 12 percent of those who left in the past decade had returned -- but usually only after acquiring a foreign passport as a hedge against 1997.
Tens of thousands of Hong Kong Chinese fled abroad after China's bloody 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown blighted their faith in living under Beijing's rule.
Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, returns to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30 next year.
